claims.statement: For eligible ordinary finite trees and ranks in the stated lower region, the fixed-selector two-for-one weighted clone graph has a matching saturating every upper clone.
claims.scope: Universal ordinary finite trees with the original fixed F(T,p), tag multiplicities w_F, all deletion pairs, and legal exactly-two-neighbor support-insertion pairs. The route's universal assertion remains unresolved; three listed T_m rows pass bounded replay.
claims.reason: retained: the route accurately presents an open universal mechanism. Copied-source replay confirms saturation and zero cut deficits for T22,p34; T60,p90; and T66,p98, with positive flow on added switch transitions. These finite cases do not prove universal Hall.

claims.statement: For the fixed original selector, active tagged independent sets biject with weighted clone layers, every old literal Delete/Retag edge projects to an underlying deletion, and the expanded graph strictly enlarges the old relation on the replayed T_m cases.
claims.scope: Ordinary finite trees at the stated ranks, with H_v=T-{v,s_v}, W_v=N(s_v)\{v}, R_v=T-N[s_v], distinct tags for each original selected leaf, and the specific bounded T_m rows recorded in EVIDENCE.json for the strictness witness.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the set-theoretic bijections, aggregate layer identity, and projection of old edges follow directly from the definitions. The source's separate order-14 tagged-fiber example was not reconstructed here; strict enlargement is instead supported by replayed switch-only flow transitions on the three listed T_m cases.

limitations: The universal weighted Hall mechanism is neither proved nor refuted.
The source replay covers only T22,p34; T60,p90; and T66,p98. The exhaustive small transition replay covers only T_m for m=1,2,3.
Hall saturation is stronger than the complete scalar aggregate inequality; a failed Hall cut alone is not an aggregate counterexample.
The expanded CB(8,92) instance remains inconclusive in the allowed sources.
The source's separate order-14 tagged-fiber example was not reconstructed in this seat.
Old tagged-relation refutations and governed RTree results do not transfer to the changed ordinary-tree graph.
